pages.quiz:
FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.

2. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. fenêtre
   B. porte
   C. chaise
   D. livre

3. When practising Persuasive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive Speaking.

4. When practising Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

5. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

6. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.

7. When practising Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading.

8. When practising Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

9. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Thank you
   C. Good night only
   D. Good morning / hello

10. When practising Reading for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for information.

11. When practising Informative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Informative Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Informative Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Informative Speaking.

12. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Informative Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.

2. D — livre

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

9. D — Good morning / hello

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Interactive speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Intensive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Informative Speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
